rationale: The hypothesis posits that SNUPN variants are loss-of-function variants typically presenting as a severe or moderate childhood-onset phenotype without dramatic sex differences. While original cohorts (such as Iruzubieta et al. 2024 and Nashabat et al. 2024) described childhood-onset muscular dystrophy with restrictive respiratory insufficiency and contractures, expanding literature demonstrates significant phenotypic and allelic divergence. Muelas et al. (2026) identified adult-onset proximo-distal and axial myopathy with early respiratory involvement mimicking inclusion body myositis. Furthermore, Okubo et al. (2026) identified biallelic SNUPN variants causing spinocerebellar ataxia with dendritic defects in Purkinje cells, where patients exhibited minimal or no overt skeletal muscle involvement. Additionally, variants are predominantly hypomorphic missense or in-frame alterations (such as p.Ile309Ser, p.Arg27Cys, p.Cys174Tyr) altering importin-beta binding, snRNP nuclear trafficking, or oligomerization without altering total protein levels, rather than classic complete loss-of-function null mutations.

evidence.text: SNUPN variants were described in five patients from two unrelated families causing a limb-girdle muscular dystrophy phenotype presenting in childhood with proximal weakness, restrictive respiratory dysfunction, contractures, and myofibrillar-like changes on biopsy. Snurportin-1 protein expression levels remained unchanged with p.Ile309Ser.

source.title: Biallelic variants in SNUPN cause a limb girdle muscular dystrophy with myofibrillar-like features
source.quote: Here, we present five patients from two unrelated families with a limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMD) phenotype carrying a biallelic variant in SNUPN gene... SNUPN patients show a similar phenotype characterized by proximal weakness starting in childhood, restrictive respiratory dysfunction and prominent contractures

evidence.text: 18 children from 15 unrelated families presented with atypical muscular dystrophy and neurological defects caused by nine hypomorphic biallelic SNUPN variants clustered predominantly in the last coding exon.

source.title: SNUPN deficiency causes a recessive muscular dystrophy due to RNA mis-splicing and ECM dysregulation
source.quote: In this study, we investigate 18 children from 15 unrelated families who present with atypical muscular dystrophy and neurological defects. Nine hypomorphic SNUPN biallelic variants, predominantly clustered in the last coding exon, are ascertained to segregate with the disease.

evidence.text: SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy (LGMDR29) extends beyond childhood onset to include adult-onset proximo-distal and axial myopathy with early respiratory involvement, as well as complex phenotypes with cataracts and spinocerebellar ataxia, driven by deleterious missense variants (p.Arg27Cys and p.Cys174Tyr) altering importin-beta binding.

source.title: SNUPN‐Related Muscular Dystrophy: Novel Phenotypic, Pathological and Functional Protein Insights
source.journal: Annals of Clinical and Translational Neurology
source.quote: SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy or LGMDR29 is a new entity that covers from a congenital or childhood onset pure muscular dystrophy to more complex phenotypes combining neurodevelopmental features, cataracts, or spinocerebellar ataxia... Here we report the first family with SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy presenting an adult-onset myopathy

evidence.text: Pathogenic variants in SNUPN caused spinocerebellar atrophy in two families with cerebellar ataxia and Purkinje cell dendritic degeneration due to disrupted global pre-mRNA splicing, with one patient displaying mild skeletal muscle changes and another showing no skeletal muscle involvement at all.

source.title: SNUPN variants cause spinocerebellar atrophy by disrupting global splicing in cerebellar Purkinje cells
source.quote: We identified pathogenic variants in the SNUPN gene in two families with spinocerebellar atrophy. One patient exhibited mild changes in skeletal muscle, while the other did not.

conflicts: The hypothesis asserts that SNUPN disease typically presents as childhood-onset limb-girdle muscular dystrophy; however, documented adult-onset myopathies with IBM-like features (Muelas et al., 2026) and primary spinocerebellar ataxia without overt muscular dystrophy (Okubo et al., 2026) contradict an exclusively or strictly typical childhood-onset muscular dystrophy presentation.

The hypothesis assumes variants are loss-of-function; however, functional studies demonstrate that pathogenic variants are hypomorphic missense alleles that alter snurportin-1 binding affinity to importin-beta or cause aberrant oligomerization/aggregation rather than complete loss of protein expression.

new_directions.question_text: What specific domain interactions govern whether a biallelic SNUPN variant produces a childhood-onset muscular dystrophy, an adult-onset axial/proximo-distal myopathy, or an isolated spinocerebellar ataxia?
new_directions.rationale: Variants identified in the importin-beta binding domain versus the C-terminal snRNP binding or oligomerization domains appear to produce divergent tissue vulnerability (skeletal muscle vs. Purkinje cells). Systematic genotype-phenotype correlation across all 12+ variants is needed.

new_directions.question_text: Are subtle subclinical Purkinje cell abnormalities and cerebellar atrophy present on brain MRI across childhood-onset LGMDR29 cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: Because Okubo et al. and Muelas et al. observed asymptomatic or symptomatic cerebellar atrophy and ataxia, prospective brain neuroimaging in pediatric LGMD patients may reveal whether cerebellar involvement is an under-recognized hallmark distinguishing LGMDR29 from other LGMDs.
